Redefine_Guidelines: Requirements must be specific and measurable; avoid vague statements.
Do not reference 'Equal or better than Predecessor' in requirement thresholds or targets.
Functional and experience improvements must have clear, quantifiable metrics.
Requests for Feature, Experience, and Warranty Improvements must be routed to Function owners (Marketing, GxD, TME) for holistic assessment.
Do not include best practices or general engineering/process instructions.

In_Scope_Product_Specific: Performance/Feature requirements specific to the product.
Quality Improvement & Serviceability specific to the product.
Telemetry requirements unique to the product.
Documentation and Process specific to the product.
Test Setup / Fixture requirements unique to the product.
Design for Manufacturing requirements unique to the product.
Cost Reduction proposals specific to the product.
Out_of_Scope_Common_Across_All_Products: Safety & Regulatory compliance (common requirements across products).
Environment & Sustainability compliance (common requirements across products).

Threshold_Target_Guidelines.Challenge: Translating subjective requirements (e.g., customer experience issues) into objective, measurable specifications is difficult.
Threshold_Target_Guidelines.Past_Practice: Use of vague statements like 'equal or better than predecessor'.
Threshold_Target_Guidelines.Proposal: State what the customer expects as a specific, observable outcome and define target and threshold with measurable criteria.

Example_Case_1_Tire_Mark.Requirement_From_Customer_Perspective: No visible tire mark on photo media.
Example_Case_1_Tire_Mark.Threshold_Acceptable_to_Ship: Minor tire mark acceptable (metric to be defined with program).
